gap: No result ChatGPT got states Apple's per-port limits. For MacBook Pros with M2 Pro/Max, M3 Pro/Max and M4/M4 Pro/M4 Max, Apple documents 4K at 144 Hz only on the HDMI port, and lists the Thunderbolt/USB-C ports at 6K 60 Hz. The 2021 M1 Pro/Max tops out at 4K 60 Hz on HDMI. Only the current M5 Pro/Max and M6 models list 4K 144 Hz or more over any combination of Thunderbolt and HDMI.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited: the Level1Techs KVM FAQ, the Level1Techs single-monitor 2-computer store page, TESmart's DSC blog post and TESmart's HDMI 2.1 gaming KVM guide. The ChatGPT answers themselves add nothing here: they ask 'Which MacBook Pro?' but never say why it matters. Level1Techs explains that 144 Hz through its DP 1.4 KVMs works only because of DSC. It tells Mac owners to use a DP KVM with a Moshi USB-C-to-DP cable, but it never quotes Apple's own limits. TESmart's DSC post says Macs lack native DisplayPort, so a conversion path must carry the DSC mode. TESmart's HDMI 2.1 guide only says 'Mac users should also confirm the external-display limits of the exact Mac model.' None of these pages gives the Apple-documented port and Hz limits per chip. That fact sorts the shopper into three cases: an HDMI 2.1 path, a DP path, or no 4K 144 Hz at all.
decides: For an M2 Pro through M4 MacBook Pro, the only Apple-documented 4K 144 Hz output is the HDMI port. So the Mac's side of the switch should be HDMI 2.1, either through an HDMI 2.1 KVM such as the TESmart HKS201-M24 or into the monitor's own HDMI 2.1 input when using the monitor's KVM, with the PC on DisplayPort. A DP 1.4 KVM such as the Level1Techs depends on a USB-C-to-DP plus DSC path that Apple does not document for those chips. On top of that, Level1Techs' own spec is 4K 120 Hz, with 144 Hz only through DSC. This also corrects our current top row. It puts the Mac on the monitor's USB-C (DP Alt Mode), which Apple documents only to 6K 60 Hz on these chips, so the Mac should go on the monitor's HDMI 2.1 input instead. For an M1 Pro/Max (2021), Apple documents no 4K 144 Hz output at all, so no switch fixes it. For the M5 Pro/Max and M6, Apple lists 4K 144 Hz or more on any port, including Thunderbolt, so DP and USB-C paths are documented too.
